question: Should the repair lane adopt this coordinated fail-closed authorization boundary on the current exact head, accepting that stale or unverifiable target, check, mutation-outcome, or state-credential evidence will block mutation and requeue work?
rationale: The implementation is technically coherent, but it changes both the trusted authorization boundary for GitHub writes and the operational availability behavior of repair apply and post-flight workflows; that tradeoff requires explicit maintainer ownership.

options.title: Approve coordinated rollout
options.body: Merge after all required checks complete on the exact head and accept fail-closed blocking and retry behavior as the intended safety contract.

options.title: Stage enforcement
options.body: Roll out authorization, apply, post-flight, and state-publication enforcement separately so each blocking mode can be observed before full activation.

options.title: Pause the branch
options.body: Retain the current mutation model until maintainers choose a different safety-versus-availability contract.

recommendation.title: Approve coordinated rollout
recommendation.body: Merge after all required checks complete on the exact head and accept fail-closed blocking and retry behavior as the intended safety contract.

likelyOwner.reason: They own the merged prerequisite and the current implementation across every central affected repair path.
